bullets.title: AI bubble unwind accelerating: 80% of AI basket in bearish TREND, semis leading lower
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags 80% of 35 AI-theme stocks now in bearish TREND, with South Korea's KOSPI down 39.1% from its peak (fell another 3.7% today) serving as the canary. Korean neocloud IPO Elice dropped 32% on debut, dragging neoclouds (CRWV, IREN, WULF, CORZ) down 2-4% in sympathy. Hedgeye's Keith McCullough sold QQQ and all Japan exposure; XLK dropped 12 spots in ETF re-rank, IGV down 12 spots in one month.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex estimates ratcheting dramatically higher; AMZN, GOOGL, META all above consensus
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley prime brokerage notes buyside expects AMZN 2027 capex ~$350B vs. consensus $285B, META $225-250B vs. $201B consensus, GOOGL ~$375B vs. $309B, MSFT >$220B. Compute shortages are favoring hyperscalers as orchestration layers with 60-70% incremental EBIT margins; MSFT Azure and AMZN AWS have both raised prices recently. AMZN power constraints are forcing NVDA racks into intermediate warehouses despite $5B+ August orders.

bullets.title: META Prometheus 1GW Ohio supercluster (~1M GPUs) confirms massive NVDA/AVGO/ANET optical networking order
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley confirms META's Prometheus supercluster in Ohio will use NVDA GB200/GB300 and Vera Rubin chips, with AVGO Jericho3, ANET 7800-series, and NVDA Spectrum-4 as the optical networking backbone. NVDA separately received $35B+ RTX PRO 5500 orders from ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent for export-compliant chips. MS also notes GOOGL TPU business is significantly underestimated, with Mizuho projecting $100B TPU revenue by 2028.

bullets.title: Housing deteriorating sharply: starts -5.2% to 1.22M, NAHB at cycle low since 2012; GDP tracking cut to 3.1%
bullets.body: September housing starts fell 5.2% m/m to 1,221k (consensus 1.31M), with single-family down 4.6% and multifamily down 6.7%; NAHB survey hit its lowest since 2012. Pending home sales dropped 7.3% m/m vs. consensus -0.5%, pointing to existing home sales below 4M annualized. Morgan Stanley cut 3Q GDP tracking from 3.2% to 3.1% on -4.0% q/q real residential investment; analysts see housing weakening further into 2027 given current rate structure.

bullets.title: Stock-bond correlation shift to neutral is bullish equities in isolation; 10yr breakeven anchored at 2.25%
bullets.body: A macro note argues the stock-bond correlation moving from negative to neutral reflects escape from liquidity-trap left-tail risk, not a structural inflation regime change — a net positive for equities even as it reduces Treasury hedge value. The 10-year breakeven is locked at 2.25%, suggesting market confidence in a 2% PCE regime. Rising term premium from higher correlation is bearish bonds but bullish equities; the skew is toward wider breakevens if the market is wrong on the Fed.

bullets.title: SPX in fragile technical position: TREND at 7,601, VIX 19 key threshold; positioning heavily short per GS
bullets.body: Hedgeye sets S&P 500 TREND support at 7,601 (Nasdaq at 26,119); VIX 19 is the threshold to avoid the 'Chop Bucket,' with Nasdaq volatility (VXN at 25.56) already inside it. Oppenheimer notes SPX needs to retake 7,700 to exit negative gamma territory; GS prime notes HF net exposure to Mag 7 at ~23% of US net (vs. >25% in 2025 peaks), sub-50% net leverage, and short exposure at 85th percentile on a 1-year basis — a positioning set that could fuel a squeeze on upside earnings surprises.

bullets.title: Energy rotating into leadership: oil up, crack spreads wide; Hedgeye shifts to energy from tech
bullets.body: WTI crude up 2%, Brent up 1.5%; propane surged ~34% in the past month signaling energy inflation. Hedgeye's McCullough added CRAK (oil refining ETF) at 100bps, sold BUG/IGV/QQQ; his 20-stock signal strength list now includes five energy names (Petrobras, Marathon, CVR Energy, PBF Energy, Valero). LNG prices (JKM) rose to ~$30, highest since 2022, on low inventories.

bullets.title: ADP private payroll 4-week average slows to +18.5K from +26.0K prior — hiring deceleration
bullets.body: ADP weekly data for the 4-week period ending Oct 3 shows private employers added an average of 18.5K jobs, down from 26.0K the prior 4-week average. The survey covers ~26M private workers and excludes federal employment. The step-down adds to a picture of softening labor demand alongside weak housing data.

bullets.title: US midterms: Democratic sweep (91% House odds per Polymarket); defense capped, tariffs past peak, AI legislation unlikely
bullets.body: Hedgeye political analyst JT Taylor's base case is Democrats win at least 225 House seats, with Senate six to seven seats within 2.7% margin. Defense budget likely lands at $1.15T base + $50-70B supplemental (not $1.5T feared). Only 20% odds AI legislation passes this Congress; tariffs are likely past peak with court challenges ongoing on IEEPA/232/301, and another wave of tariff refunds is possible in 1H27.

bullets.title: Gartner vs. MS Spark: only 13% of CIOs see significant AI value, but private-company ARR ramps suggest ROI is real
bullets.body: Gartner data shows only 13% of CIOs see significant AI value with a 20% use-case success rate, though 71% plan agentic AI deployment within 12 months. Contrasting this, Morgan Stanley Spark finds AI ROI materializing in private companies with extraordinary ARR ramps (Fireworks $100M to $1B in 8 months; Cognition $1B in under 2 years). The divergence frames the key bull/bear debate heading into hyperscaler earnings.

bullets.title: Goldman warns grid bottlenecks could stall AI expansion; power demand surging
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs flagged that grid bottlenecks could stall the AI infrastructure buildout as power demand surges; ~35 data center ballot measures are on the Nov 3 ballot across 8 states. ABB (European DC power equipment) reported +40% orders but stock fell 5%; Schneider Electric showed the same pattern — a negative read-through for US AI infrastructure plays.

bullets.title: Networking VAR checks remain strong: CSCO +13% y/y, FFIV +8-9%, ANET solid — enterprise budgets intact
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley 3Q26 VAR checks show broad networking momentum: FFIV growing ~8-9% y/y vs. historical 1-2% on multi-cloud demand (expected to beat by 3.5-4% with ~$940M FQ4 revenue); CSCO at ~13% y/y using aggressive discounting to defend share; ANET reseller growth ranging low-teens to ~30% y/y with pricing stability. Enterprise budgets are stretched but Q4 budget flush is unlikely.

bullets.title: Salesforce acquires Braze for $5.66B (58-60% premium); antitrust risk flagged, early buyside feedback mixed
bullets.body: CRM signed a definitive agreement to acquire Braze at $47.50/share ($5.66B EV, ~5-6x forward revenue), funded entirely with cash (~4 months of FY27 FCF). No change to FY27 guidance or FY30 framework; deal closes in CRM FY28. GS flags antitrust risk given Braze lists Salesforce and Adobe as key competitors; CRM IR VP is departing and early buyside feedback is mixed-to-negative. CRM stock down ~2.9% premarket.

bullets.title: NFLX down 36% from highs, engagement weakening; WSJ 'streaming wall' narrative mounting into earnings
bullets.body: Netflix global Top-10 viewing hours fell 11% in Q3, with its share of TV viewing down 1 point y/y in July per Hedgeye. WSJ reports a 'streaming wall' as engagement slides toward TikTok/YouTube. Multiple talent departures (CCO, Head of Film, Live Experiences) and a ~1K layoff add to skepticism. The stock trades at ~19x '27E EPS after falling ~23% YTD; 22V Research sees a contrarian setup at $70 (~22x P/E at 5-year lows) and suggests a covered strangle strategy.

bullets.title: Semis bifurcating: HDD/storage (WDC, STX) bullish on AI demand; NVDA, AMD neocloud narrative under pressure
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reinstates STX as Top Pick with 10-12% above-consensus Dec Q EPS and 80%+ base-case upside; WDC preferred as tactical long on asymmetric HDD margin setup (through-cycle margins could reach 45-50%). UBS models WDC Sept Q revenue/EPS of $4.27B/$4.40 vs. street $4.14B/$4.09, and Dec Q $5.03B/$5.93 vs. street $4.56B/$4.76. In contrast, Hedgeye removes NVDA long and AMD estimate confusion (prior substrate model included ~1.4M Venice CPU units miscategorized as GPU) adds uncertainty.

bullets.title: TXN data center exposure +73-75% y/y; analog buyers pre-buying on supply shortage fears
bullets.body: UBS expects TXN CQ3 revenue/EPS at high end of guidance ($6.05B/$2.48) with CQ4 guidance likely $5.8-5.9B above street (~$5.7B). Data center growth expected at 73%/75% y/y in CQ3/CQ4; analog purchasers reportedly worried about supply shortages and pre-buying, favoring TXN. Wolfe adds GFS to its Alpha List on tightening mature node supply with government fab partnership adding 50-75c EPS accretion.

bullets.title: China Q3 GDP 4.6% YTD; manufacturing utilization at post-COVID low of 73.3%; fiscal stimulus fading
bullets.body: China's Q3 GDP print of 4.6% YTD rules out additional fiscal stimulus this year; manufacturing capacity utilization fell to a new post-COVID low of 73.3%. Beijing is expected to prioritize SOE consolidation in autos and steel for 2027 while AI-focused spending runs its course in early 2027. Tariffs are likely not the main inflation driver; peak price-level effect is likely behind us per 22V Research.

bullets.title: Multi-manager hedge fund AUM grew $314B→$536B since 2022; firm count up 39→56; AI crowding a key GS topic
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs prime notes the multi-manager universe expanded from 39 to 56 firms with AUM growing from $314B to $536B and headcount topping 27,000 since 2022. GS is hosting a flow & positioning webinar Oct 21 to specifically discuss AI crowding durability, rates/inflation repricing, and recent risk reduction across global equities — suggesting the street is actively monitoring positioning stress in the AI trade.

bullets.title: AAPL downgraded to Hold at Loop Capital (PT cut $370→$330); Duo delivery dates pulled in for Oct 28 event
bullets.body: Loop Capital's Ananda Baruah downgraded AAPL to Hold from Buy with the price target cut to $330 from $370. Separately, Morgan Stanley notes AAPL is moving iPhone Duo delivery dates forward with an Oct 28 event expected to debut the first touchscreen MacBook and M6 14-inch MacBook Pro — a near-term product catalyst.

bullets.title: US power/nuclear sentiment: SMR downgraded at Barclays (-7.6%); OKLO -3.7%; nuclear ballot measures Nov 3
bullets.body: SMR was downgraded by Barclays and fell 7.6% premarket; OKLO dropped 3.7%. Across the 52-week extreme list, SMR is down 87.5% YTD and OKLO down 83.3% YTD. ATRL announced an MOU with India State and Hoosier Energy for eight potential CANDU reactors (6 GW capacity). Thirty-five data center ballot measures are on the Nov 3 ballot across 8 states, with Ohio holding >50% of current projects — political risk to AI/nuclear infrastructure sentiment is rising.
